Reidoth.name: Reidoth
Reidoth.text:
@UUID[Actor.pbsoReidoth00000]{Reidoth}

Reidoth è un druido esperto delle terre selvagge e delle rovine di Thundertree. Prudente e attento agli equilibri naturali, può fornire informazioni preziose sui pericoli della zona.

Redbrand Ruffian.name: Malvivente dei Marchi Rossi
Redbrand Ruffian.text:
@UUID[Actor.pbsoRedbrandRuff]{Malvivente dei Marchi Rossi}

I malviventi dei Marchi Rossi sono esecutori spietati abili nell'intimidazione e nella violenza. Lavorano per denaro e non hanno scrupoli.

Bandit.name: Bandito
Bandit.text:
@UUID[Actor.n4TEv7inVUkyZviN]{Bandito}

I banditi si riuniscono in bande e sono talvolta guidati da scagnozzi, veterani o incantatori. Privi di scrupoli, lavorano per chiunque paghi di più e sfruttano imboscate, intimidazione e superiorità numerica.

Nascondiglio dei Marchi Rossi: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoRedbrandsHid.JournalEntryPage.phxAu1Xnd1nxSSGG]{Nascondiglio dei Marchi Rossi}

Skeleton.name: Scheletro
Skeleton.text:
@UUID[Actor.nU8GN8La8DCt8SDb]{Scheletro}

Gli scheletri sono ossa rianimate da necromanti, maledizioni o spiriti maligni. Che siano resti antichi o cadaveri recenti ormai spogliati della carne, obbediscono ciecamente agli ordini del loro creatore e combattono finché non vengono ridotti in pezzi.

Riferimenti

Droop.name: Droop
Droop.text:
@UUID[Actor.pbsoDroop0000000]{Droop}

I goblin sono piccoli umanoidi egoisti che vivono in caverne e strutture abbandonate. Droop è un goblin prigioniero che i personaggi possono incontrare nel Castello Fierefauci.

Riferimenti

Nascondiglio dei Marchi Rossi: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoRedbrandsHid.JournalEntryPage.NJsdEEfbqkVh1Zbt]{Nascondiglio dei Marchi Rossi}

Zeond.name: Zeond
Zeond.text:
@UUID[Actor.bwtkdzavdNHISgp4]{Zeond}

I quasit infestano i Piani Inferiori. Fisicamente deboli, si tengono nell’ombra a complottare e preferiscono attaccare mentre sono &Reference[invisible]{invisibili}. Zeond è un quasit che serve come famiglio del mago Iarno Albrek nei Sotterranei di Tresendar.

Riferimenti

Nascondiglio dei Marchi Rossi: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoRedbrandsHid.JournalEntryPage.7a8bh0HomdlNyHw9]{Nascondiglio dei Marchi Rossi}

Twig Blight.name: Piaga dei Rami
Twig Blight.text:
@UUID[Actor.pbsoTwigBlight00]{Piaga dei Rami}

Una piaga dei rami è una pianta risvegliata che assomiglia a un arbusto legnoso che può tirare fuori i suoi rami dalla terra e muoversi. Questi esseri oscuri servono il semidio Gulthias.

Ash Zombie.text:
@UUID[Actor.pbsoAshZombie000]{Zombie Cinereo}

Questi zombi furono creati dalla devastazione magica quando il Monte Hotenow eruttò decenni fa. Le ceneri dell'esplosione vulcanica miscelate con energia necrotica rianimarono i corpi dei morti.

Cultist.name: Cultista
Cultist.text:
@UUID[Actor.qkLNA1lKMMJpxuWg]{Cultista}

I cultisti giurano fedeltà ai poteri oscuri come principi elementali, signori dei demoni, diavoli o antiche entità. Eseguono riti oscuri e spargono sangue in onore delle loro divinità malvagie.

Venomfang.name: Venomfang
Venomfang.text:
@UUID[Actor.85ahD1jEo9B3POaQ]{Venomfang}

Venomfang è un giovane drago verde, astuto, velenoso e manipolatore. Preferisce ottenere vantaggi con menzogne e intimidazioni prima di ricorrere alla forza, ma resta un avversario letale.

Needle Blight.name: Piaga degli Aghi
Needle Blight.text:
@UUID[Actor.pbsoNeedleBlight]{Piaga degli Aghi}

Nell'ombra di una foresta, le piaghe degli aghi potrebbero essere scambiate a distanza per arbusti contorti. Questi servitori del Gulthias sparano spine ai passanti non appena li avvistano.

Riferimenti

Giant Spider.name: Ragno Gigante
Giant Spider.text:
@UUID[Actor.v99wOosUJjUgcUNF]{Ragno Gigante}

Per intrappolare la sua preda, il ragno gigante tesse elaborate ragnatele o spara fili appiccicosi. Questi predatori sotterranei sono tra gli aracnidi più temibili nell'Underdark.

Riferimenti

Otyugh.name: Otyugh
Otyugh.text:
@UUID[Actor.jcZblJ6lqtW0ePxe]{Otyugh}

Un otyugh è una grottesca creatura bulbosa che si sposta su tre robuste zampe. Questi spazzini vivono tra i rifiuti e i resti organici, digerendo praticamente qualsiasi sostanza organica.

Riferimenti

Sonno di Zorzula: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoZorzulasRest.JournalEntryPage.iwHTEsBgYwxCMM94]{Sonno di Zorzula}

Umber Hulk.name: Hulk del Crepuscolo
Umber Hulk.text:
@UUID[Actor.pbsoUmberHulk000]{Hulk del Crepuscolo}

Gli hulk del crepuscolo sono creature aberranti deformate dall’influenza del Reame Remoto. Massicci, brutali e difficili da abbattere, avanzano come strumenti viventi di distruzione, guidati da impulsi che le menti comuni non possono comprendere.

Riferimenti

Campo di Battaglia del Lamento: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoWailingBattl.JournalEntryPage.z8reIBUReL7uL5iX]{Campo di Battaglia del Lamento}

Nycaloth.name: Nycaloth
Nycaloth.text:
@UUID[Actor.pbsoNycaloth0000]{Nycaloth}

I nycaloth sono le truppe d’urto aeree d’élite degli yugoloth. Questi temibili immondi alati colpiscono con rapidità, poi usano la magia innata per diventare &Reference[invisible]{invisibili} o confondere i nemici con illusioni.

Riferimenti

Campo di Battaglia del Lamento: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoWailingBattl.JournalEntryPage.D4XmfNMw2C1zBwO5]{Campo di Battaglia del Lamento}

Ochre Jelly.name: Melma Ocra
Ochre Jelly.text:
@UUID[Actor.xBhG7Dos3tkg9jWz]{Melma Ocra}

Una melma ocra è una fanghiglia giallastra che può scivolare sotto le porte e attraverso fessure strette. Questi predatori privi di forma corrodono la carne organica con i loro acidi.

Riferimenti

Caverna dell'Onda Tonante: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoWaveEchoCave.JournalEntryPage.m2AnHrxvpM0pUPpF]{Caverna dell'Onda Tonante}

Caverna dell'Onda Tonante: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoWaveEchoCave.JournalEntryPage.vkS4WjbQwjTFKBoh]{Caverna dell'Onda Tonante}

Ogre Zombie.name: Zombie d'Orco
Ogre Zombie.text:
@UUID[Actor.RenLfmDT2XlbCF4x]{Zombie d'Orco}

Da qualche parte nell'oscurità si sente un gemito gorgogliante. Una forma barcolla alla vista. Questo zombie d'orco, di dimensioni ben superiori a un normale zombie, si trascina verso qualsiasi creatura vivente.

Riferimenti

Caverna dell'Onda Tonante: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoWaveEchoCave.JournalEntryPage.PS7ZZ8FNPDqIKK1B]{Caverna dell'Onda Tonante}

Violet Fungus.name: Fungo Viola
Violet Fungus.text:
@UUID[Actor.7EmUVycEASn7SFL0]{Fungo Viola}

Un fungo viola è un organismo sotterraneo apparentemente innocuo finché una creatura non gli si avvicina troppo. Allora agita i suoi tentacoli putrescenti, facendo marcire la carne al minimo tocco. Una creatura uccisa da un fungo viola si decompone rapidamente; un nuovo fungo viola germoglia dal cadavere in putrefazione e raggiunge la piena taglia in [[/gmroll 2d6]] giorni.

Riferimenti

Caverna dell'Onda Tonante: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoWaveEchoCave.JournalEntryPage.jb8k7zK2zc91RDLL]{Caverna dell'Onda Tonante}

Giant Constrictor Snake.name: Serpente Costrittore Gigante
Giant Constrictor Snake.text:
@UUID[Actor.NpvwE1feOHyEqAbP]{Serpente Costrittore Gigante}

Il serpente costrittore gigante uccide avvolgendo la preda nelle sue spire e stritolandola con forza implacabile. È particolarmente pericoloso in acqua, paludi o vegetazione fitta.

Riferimenti

Caverna dell'Onda Tonante: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoWaveEchoCave.JournalEntryPage.tSgLovz8boD8RgYp]{Caverna dell'Onda Tonante}

Mormesk the Wraith.name: Mormesk il Fantasma
Mormesk the Wraith.text:
@UUID[Actor.pbsoMormeskTheWr]{Mormesk il Fantasma}

Mormesk è uno spettro potente, l'anima di un mago che un tempo viveva nella Caverna dell'Onda Tonante. La sua essenza è malvagità incarnata, concentrata in una forma incorporea.

Riferimenti

Caverna dell'Onda Tonante: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoWaveEchoCave.JournalEntryPage.3O9PWNjTxkdHk8bd]{Caverna dell'Onda Tonante}

Giant Octopus.name: Polpo Gigante
Giant Octopus.text:
@UUID[Actor.p9Xnr820UAZBOIVN]{Polpo Gigante}

Il polpo gigante è un predatore marino intelligente e sfuggente. Usa tentacoli poderosi, mimetismo e inchiostro per intrappolare le prede o fuggire dai nemici.

Riferimenti

Caverna dell'Onda Tonante: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoWaveEchoCave.JournalEntryPage.8Bj7MPxoFccBLXIL]{Caverna dell'Onda Tonante}

Brughor Axe-Biter.name: Brughor Axe-Biter
Brughor Axe-Biter.text:
@UUID[Actor.pbsoBrughorAxebi]{Brughor Axe-Biter}

Gli orchi sono razziatori robusti con canini prominenti simili a zanne. Brughor Morsodiscure è un feroce guerriero orco che guida il suo gruppo con brutalità ineguagliabile.

Riferimenti

Tor della Viverna: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoWyvernTor000.JournalEntryPage.QTwTwD5nJuHDiiRz]{Tor della Viverna}

Bessie (Giant Badger).name: Bessie (Tasso Gigante)
Bessie (Giant Badger).text:
@UUID[Actor.cJGY1ZywUOo6heNR]{Bessie (Tasso Gigante)}

Bessie è un tasso gigante, una creatura robusta e scavatrice che può diventare sorprendentemente aggressiva se minacciata. In mano a un DM, può essere un alleato insolito, una cavalcatura o una presenza memorabile.

Riferimenti

Sonno di Zorzula: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoZorzulasRest.JournalEntryPage.jjovjWoBxmYmBzH2]{Sonno di Zorzula}

Hjoldak Hollowhelm.name: Hjoldak Hollowhelm
Hjoldak Hollowhelm.text:
@UUID[Actor.pbsoHjoldakHollo]{Hjoldak Hollowhelm}

Hjoldak Fortecasco è un wight cinereo che si è risvegliato vicino a una vena di cristallo intrisa di potere aberrante. Come tutti i wight cinerei, è sia potente che malevolo.

Riferimenti

Sonno di Zorzula: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoZorzulasRest.JournalEntryPage.vU8dDpPmNlmhFBDo]{Sonno di Zorzula}

Otyugh Mutate.name: Otyugh Mutante
Otyugh Mutate.text:
@UUID[Actor.pbsoOtyughMutate]{Otyugh Mutante}

Sorto da cumuli di carogne e rifiuti esposti all’energia del Reame Remoto, un otyugh mutante sviluppa placche chitinose nere come la pece sugli arti. Queste contrastano con la carne traslucida e quasi spettrale, che lascia intravedere il luridume virulento divorato di recente.

Mutanti

Una creatura esposta alla strana energia del Reame Remoto rischia di sviluppare mutazioni. La trasformazione riscrive il corpo e l’essenza della creatura, imprimendole caratteristiche innaturali e spesso poteri psionici.

Alcune creature sono particolarmente inclini a mutare, come il @UUID[Actor.pbsoCloakerMutat]{mantello}. Un otyugh mutante conserva la fame e la resistenza dell’otyugh comune, ma le unisce a tratti aberranti che lo rendono ancora più ripugnante e pericoloso.

Riferimenti

Sonno di Zorzula: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoZorzulasRest.JournalEntryPage.iwHTEsBgYwxCMM94]{Sonno di Zorzula}

Fiendish Auger.name: Trivella Fiendish
Fiendish Auger.text:
@UUID[Actor.pbsoFiendishAuge]{Trivella Fiendish}

Una trivella fiendish viene creata quando uno spirito malvagio entra in un trapano da escavazione, facendo ardere la massiccia punta a spirale di fuoco infernale. Alimentate dall’aggressività dello spirito che le anima, queste macchine possono perforare rapidamente anche la roccia solida.

Chi impiega una trivella fiendish deve però sorvegliarla con attenzione. Senza ordini chiari, la macchina scava in modo indiscriminato, trasformando uno strumento utile in una minaccia incontrollabile.

Riferimenti

Sonno di Zorzula: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoZorzulasRest.JournalEntryPage.xc8QtXYkMu6R60NN]{Sonno di Zorzula}

Wandering Monsters.name: Wandering Monsters
Wandering Monsters.description: If the characters spend a long time in an area, you can check for wandering monsters by rolling a [[/r 1d20]]. On a roll of 17–20, an encounter takes place. Conversely, if the players seem restless, you can decide that an encounter occurs.

Goblin Mischief.name: Goblin Mischief
Goblin Mischief.description: Whenever the characters finish investigating one of the goblin crime scenes, consult this table to see what occurs.

1-1.description: A @UUID[Actor.pbsoGoblinPsiCom]{goblin psi commander} is lighting small fires around the Alderleaf Farm, and these fires threaten to set the crops ablaze.

2-2.description: Four @UUID[Actor.TjWQOgI3A4UAl7lC]{goblins} surround an older human woman and attempt to steal her purse. The @UUID[Actor.SqZRuJ8lt2KGJBbq]{woman} aggressively fights the goblins.

3-3.description: Three @UUID[Actor.TjWQOgI3A4UAl7lC]{goblins} stole a @UUID[Actor.y8sRU8Ks2lcrGsaf]{goat} and are attempting to run away with it. The goat, however, refuses to move.

4-4.description: A pair of @UUID[Actor.pbsoGoblinPsiBra]{goblin psi brawlers} are hiding in the trees of the Edermath Orchard. The goblins are using their telepathy to masquerade as ghosts and scare off others so they can steal apples uninterrupted.

5-5.description: Five @UUID[Actor.TjWQOgI3A4UAl7lC]{goblins} fling refuse at passers-by from the alley behind Stonehill Inn.

6-6.description: Three @UUID[Actor.TjWQOgI3A4UAl7lC]{goblins} splash paint across the side of Harbin Wester’s home

7-7.description: Shingles from the roof of the Sleeping Giant are flying toward a group of five confused @UUID[Actor.SqZRuJ8lt2KGJBbq]{miners.} Unbeknownst to them, a cackling @UUID[Actor.pbsoGoblinPsiCom]{goblin psi commander} on the tavern roof is the source of the mischief.

8-8.description: One @UUID[Actor.pbsoGoblinPsiBra]{goblin psi brawler} and two @UUID[Actor.TjWQOgI3A4UAl7lC]{goblins} are camped at the entrance to Triboar Trail, waiting to ambush unsuspecting travelers.

9-9.description: Two @UUID[Actor.TjWQOgI3A4UAl7lC]{goblins} released two @UUID[Actor.Bupo3E9X5Ptx6XeT]{draft horses} that are now running rampant across town.

10-10.description: Two @UUID[Actor.pbsoGoblinPsiBra]{goblin psi brawlers} have poorly disguised themselves as children and are pestering a baker for sweets near the Stonehill Inn.

Crypt Hauntings.name: Crypt Hauntings
Crypt Hauntings.description:
If the characters take a long rest in the crypt, you can have a random crypt haunting appear at that location anytime during their rest. These spontaneous hauntings can’t be put to rest, but they don’t need to be quelled to purify the crypt. Once the crypt is purified no haunts ever occur there.

These hauntings are disturbing, and the fifth and sixth options on the table below involve body horror. Check your players’ comfort level before including these hauntings in your game; you can roll a d4 instead or lock (  ) those results.

1-1.description: Each character feels a creeping sensation along their scalp, as of probing tentacles seeking a weak spot in their skull.

2-2.description: The ghostly image of an elderly dwarf in priestly vestments wanders around as though in shock, gripping a battleaxe stained with purple ichor.

3-3.description: Each character gains a nagging suspicion that mind flayers are currently invading some sacred or secret place important to that character, such as a childhood home.

4-4.description: Each character hears low muttering in Dwarvish that repeats, “The brain eaters have come! Save us! If you cannot save us, avenge us!”

5-5.description: A ghostly image of one character (determined randomly) lies on the floor, their skull cracked open and their brain removed. The image does nothing but twitch and drool.

6-6.description: The ghostly image of a dwarf zombie lurches from a wall, puts a rotted finger to its lips, then uses its other hand to peel back its ribcage and reveal a gem hidden in its chest cavity. The zombie then disappears into the wall. This image repeats every few minutes, but the ghostly zombie comes from a different section of the wall each time.

Crystal Images.name: Crystal Images
Crystal Images.description: The three newer crystals are results 1, 2, and 3; if a character examines the newer crystals, use only those results. There are 40 crystals in this room, though many of the older crystals impart the same scenes.

1-1.description: A mind flayer holding a disembodied head chants over a large pool filled with a pink, quivering gelatinous mass (the brain pool in @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoCh7illithino.Yc2CgRktnHDElf1R]{area X15}). Two other mind flayers are nearby, but their features are unclear. A strange, jagged portal appears behind the trio and then disappears. The mind flayer is visibly frustrated by this result, telepathically intoning, “We will try again. In Ilvaash’s name, we will keep trying.”

2-2.description: A mind flayer with tentacles at the ends of its arms lashes a hand-tentacle across the face of a shriveled mind flayer with a single, staring eye, drawing blood. Several strange pods line the walls (@UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoCh7illithino.oo9ELp7kXbqSA9KS]{area X12}). A mental message rings out, “You will obey, or the Far Realm shall consume what mind you have left, weakling.”

3-3.description: A beholder floats in a room with stained surgical slabs (@UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoCh7illithino.YfeV9foQJa7ZSvOQ]{area X10}), addressing a mind flayer on a rust-colored floating disk. The mind flayer raises its hands and the beholder shudders, its eye stalks writhing. The beholder telepathically squeals, “I will serve! I will serve!” (This scene shows the creation of Golcuus the oculorb, which lairs in @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoCh7rifts0000.JournalEntryPage.QEoHb6Yvc5hnX6hH]{area L7.})

4-4.description: A mind flayer wearing a scarlet robe with a high collar directs a battle in a long, descending hall lined with dwarven statues (@UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoCh6talhunder.JournalEntryPage.yxyyMpycWR6HIKnx]{area T2} of Talhundereth). Mind flayers fight fiercely against dwarves.

5-5.description: Three mind flayers sort through a bin of gems near a stone table. One selects the gem that contains this memory. (This scene takes place in @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoCh6crypttalh.JournalEntryPage.jwOdV6Q98BOi9VyA]{area P3} in the Crypt of the Talhund.)

20-20.description: This crystal isn’t a repository of memories, but a @UUID[Item.pbsoHeightenedMi]{heightened mind crystal}. Reroll this result if the characters have already found this crystal.

6-19.description: Choose a random area in @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoCh6gibbetcro]{Gibbet Crossing} and describe a short scene where [[1d4]] mind flayers capture and consume one of the area’s former denizens (drow, duergar, or deep gnomes).

Tunnel Encounters.name: Tunnel Encounters
Tunnel Encounters.description:
After each hour the characters spend in the tunnel, roll 1d20 and consult the Tunnel Encounters table to determine whether the party has a random encounter.

If the party is using a light source, creatures that encounter them almost certainly know the characters are coming and set up an ambush or otherwise prepare for the fight.

3-3.description: [[/r 1d6]] @UUID[Actor.8pX2JhWUpTNNRBVx]{gibbering mouthers} lie in wait for prey.

4-4.description: An @UUID[Actor.pbsoIntellectDev]{intellect devourer} inhabits a @UUID[Actor.pbsoQuaggoth0000]{quaggoth}; the intellect devourer seeks another host.

5-5.description: A lost and angry @UUID[Actor.pbsoFomorian0000]{fomorian} wanders the Underdark.

6-6.description: [[/r 1d4 + 1]] @UUID[Actor.pbsoHookHorror00]{hook horrors} climb on the tunnel ceiling.

7-7.description: [[/r 1d6]] @UUID[Actor.pbsoQuaggoth0000]{quaggoths} led by a @UUID[Actor.pbsoQuaggothThon]{quaggoth thonot} are searching for a missing tribe member who’s been acting strangely.

8-8.description: [[/r 1d6]] @UUID[Actor.pbsoTroglodyte00]{troglodytes} and a @UUID[Actor.pbsoBarlgura0000]{barlgura} are looking for a fight.

9-9.description: A patch of [[/r 2d4]] @UUID[Actor.TaK6nQMGqZ0y8gt7]{shriekers} blocks the way ahead; if they shriek, roll @UUID[Macro.8kMkMi53MikZCoo7]{1d8 on this table} to see what creatures come to investigate.

Endless Void Nodules.name: Endless Void Nodules
Endless Void Nodules.description: Whenever the characters arrive on a nodule, roll twice on the Endless Void Nodules table to randomly determine two other nodules that are near enough for the characters to see and reach by flying through the void. Reroll any result that gives the characters’ current nodule. If you roll the same result twice, only that single nodule is in view at the time.

8-8.description: @UUID[JournalEntry.pbsoIlvaashsAnim]{Ilvaash's Anima} (reroll if the characters haven’t already visited at least five other nodules)

Stage 1 Transformation Effects.name: Stage 1 Transformation Effects
Stage 1 Transformation Effects.description: The Far Realm reaches out to the character in one of the following ways:

1-1.description: The character awakens from nightmares to an audible, disturbing voice urging them and those around them to go to a particular place or perform a particular act.

2-2.description: The character and those around them hear whispers of bizarre conspiracies or nonsense.

3-3.description: The character recognizes disturbing words now and then in languages they otherwise don’t understand.

4-4.description: The character notices strange patterns in everyday items and events.

5-5.description: The character discovers unfamiliar objects in familiar places.

6-6.description: The character occasionally hears an unfamiliar voice come from their throat when they try to speak.

Stage 2 Transformation Effects.name: Stage 2 Transformation Effects
Stage 2 Transformation Effects.description: The power of the Far Realm begins to alter the character’s body in one of the following unpredictable ways:

1-1.description: A body part temporarily moves or turns 360 degrees.

2-2.description: The character grows one or more eyes or mouths that are not under their control.

3-3.description: The character notices that strange bone protrusions occasionally ripple under their skin.

4-4.description: The character sprouts a tentacle that occasionally picks up Tiny objects.

Stage 3 Transformation Effects.name: Stage 3 Transformation Effects
Stage 3 Transformation Effects.description: Void energy begin to seep into the character’s soul in one of the following ways:

1-1.description: Aberrations view the character as one of their own.

2-2.description: Items tied to the Far Realm hum, glow, or vibrate when the character is nearby.

3-3.description: The character develops an unwanted craving, such as for raw meat, spoiled food, insects, hair, or fingernails.

4-4.description: The character occasionally looks down to discover writing or drawings in their handwriting or style, but that they are certain they didn’t create.

5-5.description: The character sometimes inadvertently communicates telepathically instead of how they normally communicate.

6-6.description: The character sometimes leaves black, sludgy handprints on things they touch.

Stage 4 Transformation Effects.name: Stage 4 Transformation Effects
Stage 4 Transformation Effects.description: The character’s connection to the Far Realm has grown to the extent that they now warp reality within 30 feet of them in one of the following ways:

2-2.description: Portable objects not being worn or carried change position.

Cask of Salted Pork.description: A cask of salted pork from the provisions being brought to Phandalin.

Keg of Strong Ale.description: A keg of strong ale from the supplies being brought to Phandalin.

Barrel of Oil.description: A barrel containing about 50 flasks of oil from the supplies being brought to Phandalin.

Jade Statuette.name: Jade Statuette
Jade Statuette.description: A jade statuette of a frog with tiny golden orbs for eyes.

Oil Flask.name: Oil Flask
Oil Flask.description:
Oil usually comes in a clay flask that holds 1 pint. As an action, you can splash the oil in this flask onto a creature within 5 feet of you or throw it up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. Make a ranged attack against a target creature or object, treating the oil as an improvised weapon.

On a hit, the target is covered in oil. If the target takes any fire damage before the oil dries (after 1 minute), the target takes an additional 5 fire damage from the burning oil. You can also pour a flask of oil on the ground to cover a 5-foot-square area, provided that the surface is level.

If lit, the oil burns for 2 rounds and deals 5 fire damage to any creature that enters the area or ends its turn in the area. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

Jeweled Gold Bracelet.description: A jeweled gold bracelet found amidst the bones of a sarcophagus in the Redbrands' Hideout in Phandalin.

Scarlet Cloak.description: A dirty scarlet cloak worn by the Redbrand Ruffians in Phandalin.

Staff of Defense.name: Staff of Defense
Staff of Defense.description:
Requires attunement.

This slender, hollow staff is made of glass yet is as strong as oak. It weighs 3 pounds. While holding the staff, you have a +1 bonus to your Armor Class.

Spells. The staff has 10 charges. While holding it, you can expend the requisite number of charges to cast one of the following spells from the staff: [[/item Mage Armor]] (1 charge) or [[/item Shield]] (2 charges).

The staff regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the staff’s last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the staff shatters and is destroyed.

Staff of Defense: AC Boost.description: While holding the staff, you have a +1 bonus to your Armor Class.

Urmon's Journal.name: Urmon's Journal
Urmon's Journal.description:
The journal of an adventurer named Urmon, found in the Redbrand's Hideout and written in Dwarvish. It conveys the following information:

More than five hundred years ago, clans of dwarves and gnomes made an agreement known as the Phandelver Pact, by which they would share a rich mine in a wondrous cavern known as Wave Echo Cave. In addition to its mineral wealth, the mine contained great magical power. Human spellcasters allied themselves with dwarves and gnomes to channel and bind that energy into a great forge called the Forge of Spells, where magic items could be crafted. Times were good, and the nearby town of Phandalin prospered as well. But disaster struck when bandits swept through the North and laid waste to all in their path.

A powerful bandit force reinforced by evil mercenary wizards attacked Wave Echo Cave to seize its riches and magic treasures. Human wizards fought alongside their dwarf and gnome allies to defend the Forge of Spells, and the ensuing spell battle destroyed much of the cavern. Few survived the cave-ins and tremors, and knowledge of the location of Wave Echo Cave was lost.

Golden Earring.description: A simple golden earring set with a tiny ruby.

Light Crossbow.name: Light Crossbow
Light Crossbow.description: A small crossbow with a wooden haft and a tense cord which is capable of firing a single bolt which can puncture even heavy armor at close range.

Longsword.name: Longsword
Longsword.description: A lengthy stright blade designed for slashing foes, the longsword is a highly versatile weapon that may also be wielded with two hands for more punishing strikes.

Nosk's Iron Key.name: Nosk's Iron Key
Nosk's Iron Key.description: An iron key found on Nosk in the Redbrand's Hideout.

Potion of Climbing.name: Potion of Climbing
Potion of Climbing.description:
The potion is separated into brown, silver, and gray layers resembling bands of stone. Shaking the bottle fails to mix the colors.

When you drink this potion, you gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed for 1 hour. During this time, you have advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks you make to climb.

Potion of Growth.name: Potion of Growth
Potion of Growth.description:
The red in the potion's liquid continuously expands from a tiny bead to color the clear liquid around it and then contracts. Shaking the bottle fails to interrupt this process.

When you drink this potion, you gain the "enlarge" effect of the @Compendium[dnd5e.spells.WahI41a3goVUg0x1]{Enlarge/Reduce} spell for 1d4 hours (no concentration required).

Shortsword.description: A medium sized blade with a firm crossguard and a leather-wrapped handle. A versatile weapon which makes up in versatility what it lacks in reach.

Spear.name: Spear
Spear.description: A gleaming steel point mouted atop a stout wooden haft, the spear may be wielded in one hand or two and can puncture through the heaviest armor with deadly force.

Talon.name: Talon
Talon.description:
Whether through demonic blessing, celestial bequeathment, crazed experiment, or skillful craft, this weapon has been enhanced to bring more bloodshed by the bearer.

This longsword rests in a dusty silver-chased scabbard and is inscribed with the name "Talon" with a hilt shaped like a bird of prey with outspread wings.

You have a bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

Traveler's Clothes.name: Traveler's Clothes
Traveler's Clothes.description: A set of clothes worn by travellers.

Well Made Light Crossbow.name: Well Made Light Crossbow
Well Made Light Crossbow.description: A small crossbow with a wooden haft and a tense cord which is capable of firing a single bolt which can puncture even heavy armor at close range. The woodwork is inlaid with silver.

Well Made Shortsword.name: Well Made Shortsword
Well Made Shortsword.description: A medium sized blade with a firm crossguard and a leather-wrapped handle. A versatile weapon which makes up in versatility what it lacks in reach. Its pommel and guard are set with semiprecious stones.

Censer.name: Censer
Censer.description: A beautiful censer found in the goblin shrine of Cragmaw Castle.

Chalice.name: Chalice
Chalice.description: A masterfully crafted chalice found in the goblin shrine of Cragmaw Castle.

Emboldening Brandy.name: Emboldening Brandy
Emboldening Brandy.description:
A character who imbibes a glass of brandy receives 1 &Reference[temporary-hit-points], but a character who drinks two glasses or more within 1 hour has the &Reference[condition=poisoned]{poisoned} condition for 1 hour.

A small cask filled with an exceptional dwarven brandy. Contains the equivalent of twenty glasses.

Gold Necklace with Emerald Pendant.name: Gold Necklace with Emerald Pendant
Gold Necklace with Emerald Pendant.description: A gold necklace with a fine emerald pendant.

Golden Elf Statuette.name: Golden Elf Statuette
Golden Elf Statuette.description:
A detect magic spell reveals that the statuette is imbued with divination magic. A non-evil creature grasping the statue can ask it a question and receive a telepathic response, as though the creature had cast augury. Once a creature has asked its question and received a response, it can never activate the statuette again.

A gold statuette of an elf, wrapped in crimson cloth.

Light Feathered Quarterstaff.name: Light Feathered Quarterstaff
Light Feathered Quarterstaff.description: A thick shaft of wood wrapped with a sturdy grip makes a highly functional weapon in addition to a stout walking stick. This quarterstaff is surprisingly light and engraved with stylized feathers.

Bloody Chain Mail.name: Bloody Chain Mail
Bloody Chain Mail.description: Made of interlocking metal rings, chain mail includes a layer of quilted fabric worn underneath the mail to prevent chafing and to cushion the impact of blows. The suit includes gauntlets.

Brass Dragon Scales.name: Brass Dragon Scales
Brass Dragon Scales.description: A strange, diamond-shaped plate of a brown-gold color. Each is about half the size of a human hand, light in weight, and as tough as iron.

Goblet Set With Moonstones.name: Goblet Set With Moonstones
Goblet Set With Moonstones.description: A silver goblet set with moonstones found in the Old Tower in the Ruins of Thundertree.

Hamun's Chest.name: Hamun's Chest
Hamun's Chest.description: A chest from within Hamun Kost's tent at the Old Owl Well.

Heavy Crossbow.name: Heavy Crossbow
Heavy Crossbow.description: A large crossbow mounted on a sturdy block of wood which is loaded using a hand crank and fires thick steel bolts with deadly acceleration that punches through armor and flesh.

Hew.name: Hew
Hew.description:
Whether through demonic blessing, celestial bequeathment, crazed experiment, or skillful craft, this weapon has been enhanced to bring more bloodshed by the bearer.

You have a bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

Runes spell out “Hew” in Dwarvish on the axe head and the rust is misleading. Hew deals maximum damage when the wielder attacks a Plant creature or an object made of wood. The axe’s creator used it for protection in the forest while he cut firewood.

Old Broken Wooden Chest.name: Old Broken Wooden Chest
Old Broken Wooden Chest.description: A broken, old wooden chest found in the Old Tower of the Ruins of Thundertree which had been made into Venomfang's lair.

You gain a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws while wearing this ring. The wearer also receives a +4 bonus to saving throws or checks made to avoid dropping or being disarmed of any item held in that hand.

Vial of Perfume.name: Vial of Perfume
Vial of Perfume.description: A fragrant commodity typically used by the wealthy.

Anvil Iron Key.name: Anvil Iron Key
Anvil Iron Key.description: An iron key with a head shaped like an anvil.

Dragonguard.name: Dragonguard
Dragonguard.description:
You have a +1 bonus to AC while wearing this armor.

This breastplate has a gold dragon motif worked into its design. Created for a human hero of old Neverwinter named Tergon, it grants its wearer advantage on saving throws against the breath weapons of Dragons.

This armor consists of a fitted metal chest piece worn with supple leather. Although it leaves the legs and arms relatively unprotected, this armor provides good protection for the wearer's vital organs while leaving the wearer relatively unencumbered.

Dragonguard Armor Boost.name: Dragonguard Armor Boost
Dragonguard Armor Boost.description: You have a +1 bonus to AC while wearing this armor.

Lightbringer.name: Lightbringer
Lightbringer.description: This weapon, known as Lightbringer, was made for a cleric of Lathander, the god of dawn. The head of the mace is shaped like a sunburst and is made of solid brass. The mace glows as bright as a torch when its wielder commands. While glowing, the mace deals an extra 1d6 damage to Undead creatures.

Spider Staff.name: Spider Staff
Spider Staff.description:
The top of this black, adamantine staff is shaped like a spider. The staff weighs 6 pounds. You must be attuned to the staff to gain its benefits and cast its spells.

The staff can be wielded as a quarterstaff. It deals 1d6 extra poison damage on a hit when used to make a weapon attack.

The staff has 10 charges, which are used to fuel the spells within it. With the staff in hand, you can use your action to cast one of the following spells from the staff if the spell is on your class’s spell list: spider climb (1 charge) or web (2 charges, spell save DC 15). No components are required.

The staff regains [[/r 1d6 + 4]] expended charges each day at dusk. If you expend the staff’s last charge, roll a [[/gmroll d20]]. On a 1, the staff crumbles to dust and is destroyed.

Nezznar attacks with the Spider Staff.

Statue's Emerald Eyes.name: Statue's Emerald Eyes
Statue's Emerald Eyes.description: An emerald eye from the statue of Dumathoin in Wave Echo Cave.

Black Leather Sack.name: Black Leather Sack
Black Leather Sack.description: A black leather sack found on a table in Wave Echo Cave that belonged to Nezznar the Spider.

Dwarven Ale Mug.name: Dwarven Ale Mug
Dwarven Ale Mug.description: A Dwarven ale mug made of hammered electrum.

Locked Iron Strongbox.description: A locked iron strongbox found in Wave Echo Cave.
